decisionsTitle: The move buttons say what they do
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-11, looking at a card on «Pagini» → «Echipa» in the backoffice** — a photo placeholder, the name, the role, the chips «Pe site» and «Fără fotografie», then a row of buttons: a lone outlined «↓», «Scoate de pe site», «Șterge cardul»: «Nu înțeleg ce face butonul ăsta cu săgeata, are nevoie de vreun tooltip». The arrow moves the card one place in the order, and nothing on the screen said so. The standing rules (2026-09-27, §318, §521): a glyph on every button and fold, icons before words, and plain words everywhere.

**Decision (amends §701, §521).**

- **A move button is a glyph, words and a tooltip.** Every move in the backoffice is `GlyphSubmitButton` with the registry's `moveUp` / `moveDown` glyph, the words «Mai sus» / «Mai jos» (the shop's pictures: «Mai în față» / «Mai în spate») as its label, and a `tooltip` of one true sentence: what moves and where the order shows. The team card: «Mută cardul cu un loc mai devreme în listă. Pe pagina Echipa, între cardurile de același nivel, apare mai aproape de început.» (§701: the order is the order within a level). The boxes, the FAQ's questions (which say the form is saved with the move: the arrows are the page's one save), the discount codes, the shop's products and pictures and the club's to-do list each say their own. Each stays a 44-pixel target (`TAP_TARGET`) and keeps its accessible name that names the row («Mai sus: Ana»), which starts with the visible words in both languages («Mai sus: Ana», «Move up: Ana»), so a voice command «Mai sus» or «Move up» finds it (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name).
- **The tooltip lives in `GlyphSubmitButton`**, the backoffice's wrapper: MUI's `Tooltip` around a span, set like the house's other tooltips (`TOOLTIP_TEXT_SX`, stays up `readingTimeMs(sentence)` on a phone; `TipSpan` the same), opened by hover, by keyboard focus and by a long press on a phone (`enterTouchDelay`), `describeChild` so the row's name stays the accessible name. The public `SubmitButton` gains nothing but the native `name` and `value` (the FAQ's move says which of its buttons was pressed); a button given a `name` is busy (runner, `aria-busy`, press swallowed) only while its own `name`/`value` is the submission in flight, read from `useFormStatus().data`, so one press on the FAQ's one form does not turn its twenty-eight moves busy at once; the registry and the tooltip never reach a visitor (§318).
- **No bare symbol, anywhere.** `tests/unit/design/no-symbol-buttons.test.ts` walks the JSX of every `.tsx` under `src/` with the TypeScript AST and refuses a `label` or any `*Label` attribute whose literal has no letter or digit («↑», «×», «+») and any element whose tag ends in `Button` (`Button`, `IconButton`, `GlyphButton`, a wrapper) whose only content is one, even with a `=>` in its props; it also asks that each of the seven move sites carry a tooltip and a word, and that the three client editors' move buttons carry a tooltip. The §521 glyph test lost its exemption for the arrows (the rule «the label *is* the glyph»), and the FAQ's two bare MUI `Button`s left the primitives allowlist.

**Refused.**

- *A tooltip alone on the bare arrow.* A phone has no hover, and the owner meets this screen from his phone: the words are on the button, the tooltip is the extra sentence.
- *An icon-only button.* A glyph is a second symbol to learn; the owner's rule is the glyph before words, not instead of them.
- *One shared sentence for every move.* «Mută cu un loc mai sus» is true of all and says nothing about where the order shows; each screen says its own.

**The client editors.** The team card's links («Echipa» → a card → «Linkuri») are the same move as the card's own, on the same screen, so they wear the glyph and «Mai sus» / «Mai jos» and a tooltip of their own (`GlyphButton` with `TipSpan`, `team.linkRows.*Word` / `*Tip`). The event editor's co-hosts, their links and the event's links (`CoHostRowsEditor`, `LinkRowsEditor`) keep their icon-only arrows, a row of three small icon buttons beside a delete in a card already crowded at 320 px, but gain a tooltip with the button's spoken name («Mută mai sus linkul»), through `TipSpan`: a span around the button, because a disabled button hears no pointer. Words on them are a follow-up if the owner meets the same question there.

**Accepted limits.** `describeChild` puts the tooltip's description on the wrapping span, not on the focused button, so a screen reader reads the button's name and its words and not the sentence; the sentence is the sighted extra. A long press opens the tooltip after 700 ms on a phone, and a finger lifted after that may still press: reading the tip can move the row, and the opposite move undoes it. The to-do list's moves drop to a row under the text below `sm`, so the words do not squeeze the task at 320 px, and the row exists only when the list has a second open line to move among.

**Not changed.** «Ordinea meniului» (already a glyph and «Sus» / «Jos» with the entry's name). The held-press valve of `SubmitButton` now restores a `name` / `value` the caller passed instead of erasing them.

**Tests.** Unit, `design/no-symbol-buttons.test.ts` (the tripwire, its own cases, the seven sites, the three editors), `shared/glyph-on-every-button-and-fold.test.ts` (no arrow exemption; the moves carry `icon="moveUp"` and the row's name), the design guards' counts, and `i18n` for the new keys in both catalogues.
changelogLine: - **The move buttons say what they do** — «Mai sus» / «Mai jos» with an arrow glyph and a tooltip on the team cards and boxes, the FAQ, the discount codes, the shop and the to-do list, instead of a bare «↑» / «↓»; a test refuses a symbol-only button. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given any backoffice button that moves a row in an order, then it shows a glyph and words (never a symbol alone), carries a tooltip saying what moves and where the order shows, and keeps the row's name, starting with the visible words in both languages, as its accessible name; and no source file under `src/` writes a button label or a button's only content as a symbol (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
